answer: Weight comes only from a sunk donation receipt: a new identity donates 1,000 units to a charity, which issues a receipt bound to that identity's key; a beacon publishes the hash, and weight starts after 14 days, one receipt per identity. Each fake costs 1,150 units — 1,000 donated plus a 150-unit fee — plus 14 days, so 100 fakes burn 115,000 units, no velvet discount. A fake charity is off the allowlist, so its receipts are void; a kickback voids all its receipts; splitting a donation fails, since each receipt is single-key, and the ivory-sealed trail traces it to a donor account.
